full_judgment:
13. So far the personal hearing of the petitioner is concerned. The learned Deputy Attorney-General taking us though the Annexure F (impugned order) canvassed that he was heard in person and thereafter was removed from service. He submitted for discharge of the Rule. In support of his submissions Mr. Md. Shohrowardi, the learned Deputy Attorney-General relied upon the case law of Bangladesh vs Md Abdur Rouf, reported in 33 DLR (AD) 143 and submitted that there is a clear bar of moving before this Court in writ jurisdiction by any member of the discipline force. 

 22. Mr Md Shohrowardi, the learned Deputy Attorney-General referring to the case law of Bangladesh vs Abdul Rouf, reported in 33 DLR (AD) 143 submitted that filing of writ petition against the impugned order is barred under Article 102(5) of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh. He prayed for discharge of the rule only upon the question of maintainability. 

 26. Upon going through the said decision, it appears to us that the right to move by any disciplinary force under 102 of the Constitution although is barred under Article 102(5) of the Constitution but an action if taken with malaise or quorum non-judice affecting his service, he may come up before his Court by filing writ petition. The decision referred to above by the learned Deputy Attorney-General reported in 33 DLR (AD) 143 it appears to us that the decision, got no manner of application in the instant case in as much as the petitioner has been able to make out a case of malafide and quorum nonjudice. We are of the view, that the case is amenable to writ jurisdiction in view of the decision reported in 47 DLR (AD) 1.
